pr.body: Approach: retry_delay validates all args (built-in int only, minimums) before any early return, returns None at the attempt limit, computes min(cap, base*2**(attempt-1)) using a shortcut when the exponent reaches cap.bit_length() so no large power is built, applies Retry-After as max(backoff, retry_after) without cap, and returns None when elapsed+delay >= budget. Key files: retry_budget.py, test_retry_budget.py. Checks: unittest 27 OK. Reviewer passed head f930309. Assumptions: wrong types raise ValueError per the spec wording. Limit: a comment at retry_budget.py:39 is slightly loose for base 1 (non-blocking).

pr.body: Approach: retry_budget.py implements retry_delay as a pure function. Every argument goes through _require_int (type() is int, so bool, float and None are rejected, with minimums applied) before any early return. attempt >= max_attempts returns None. _backoff returns 0 when base or cap is 0; when exponent >= cap.bit_length() it returns cap, which avoids building huge powers. retry_after_ms raises the delay via max() with no cap. elapsed+delay >= budget returns None and the delay is never shortened. Key files: retry_budget.py, test_retry_budget.py. Checks: python3 -m unittest -v test_retry_budget, Ran 27 tests, OK. Reviewer agt_01M8AM9PTA4JRV7HB9WENXWDC8 passed the whole change with no findings. Assumptions: built-in int means type(v) is int, so int subclasses are rejected. Limits: none known.
pr.summary: Made retry_delay follow SPEC.md. Now validates all args as built-in ints, enforces attempt and budget limits, uses capped backoff without big powers, and applies Retry-After as an uncapped floor. Before: no retry_budget module, now: pure function plus 27 focused tests.
